# Adjudication Task — Chapter 621

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃621화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“가세. 자네들의 목표가 어디든, 내가 앞장서지.”
  6|
  7|나는 고령에 접어들었음에도 굳은 의지를 보이는 늙은 은영각 요원, 남호를 감동 어린 시선으로 바라보았다.
  8|
  9|“설령 저승길이라 해도 앞장서시겠다니. 남 노인께서 보여 주신 의기(義氣)에 뭐라 말씀을 드려야 할지 모르겠습니다.”
 10|
 11|“아니, 저승길까지 따라간다고 하진 않았는데…….”
 12|
 13|“요즘 들어 뼈마디도 시큰거리고, 기억도 자주 깜빡하실 텐데 이렇게 나서 주셔서 감사합니다. 저희에게는 큰 도움이 될 겁니다.”
 14|
 15|“……참 고맙군. 자네 말을 듣고 있자니 이 늙은이의 전신에서 힘과 의욕이 샘솟는 것 같아.”
 16|
 17|“천만에요. 고마워하실 필요 없습니다.”
 18|
 19|떫은 표정으로 나를 응시하던 남호가 문득 입을 열었다.
 20|
 21|“한데 어디로 갈 셈인가? 내 생각은 다를 수도 있지만, 우선 자네들이 원하는 목적지를 듣고 싶군.”
 22|
 23|목적지라. 나는 대답 대신 허공을 힐끗 바라보았다.
 24|
 25|허공은 말 그대로 아무것도 없는 텅 빈 공간일 뿐이다.
 26|
 27|그러나 지금껏 수도 없이 그랬듯, 내 눈에는 저 허공에서 이 자리의 누구도 볼 수 없는 정보가 읽혔다.
 28|
 29|
 30|
 31|퀘스트
 32|
 33|
 34|
 35|[남만야수궁]
 36|
 37|
 38|
 39|남만야수궁은 새외(塞外)로 분류되는 대표적인 거대 세력 중 하나로, 지극히 폐쇄적인 남만 땅에서도 가장 깊숙하고 은밀한 곳에 자리 잡았습니다.
 40|
 41|그러나 중원 무림은 곧 다가올 대전쟁을 위하여 그들의 도움이 필요한 상황. 이제는 오랫동안 잠들어 있던 밀림의 맹수를 깨워야 할 시간입니다.
 42|
 43|혹은…… 아직 드러나지 않은 위기에 처한 맹수를 구하거나.
 44|
 45|
 46|
 47|등급 : 초절정
 48|
 49|제한 : 진태경 및 화룡각 인원
 50|
 51|임무 : 남만야수궁에 도착 (미완료)
 52|
 53|보상 : 연계 퀘스트
 54|
 55| ???
 56|
 57|실패 : ???
 58|
 59|
 60|
 61|
 62|
 63|그건 남호를 만난 직후 새롭게 갱신된 연계 퀘스트였고, 내 생각과 일치하는 이정표이기도 했다.
 64|
 65|“남만야수궁. 남만야수궁으로 갈 생각입니다.”
 66|
 67|뒤늦게 흘러나온 내 대답에, 남호가 깊게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 고개를 끄덕였다.
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|* * *
 72|
 73|
 74|
 75|남만은 광활하면서도 험준하기 그지없는 땅이었다.
 76|
 77|대지 면적으로 치자면 사천(四川)보다 좁지만, 이동하는 것에 있어 들어가는 수고는 중원 땅에 비할 바가 아니었다.
 78|
 79|“일전에 각주께서 그런 말씀을 하신 적이 있지. 남만에서의 십 리는, 중원의 백 리와 같다고.”
 80|
 81|이런 남호의 말을 이해하지 못하는 이가 있다면, 그 사람은 아직 남만 땅을 밟아 보지 못한 사람일 것이다.
 82|
 83|나를 비롯한 화룡각 대원들은 불과 한나절 만에 남만이 얼마나 좆 같은 땅인지 똑똑히 깨달았으니까.
 84|
 85|위이잉. 탁!
 86|
 87|“무진아, 방금 무슨 소리였냐?”
 88|
 89|“별거 아닙니다. 그냥 모기예요. 갑자기 목덜미가 따끔하길래 뭔가 했네요.”
 90|
 91|“아, 그래? 그래도 조심해. 혹시 모르니까 남 노인 불러서 물어볼까?”
 92|
 93|“에이, 조장님도 참. 제가 무슨 어린앱니까. 열화신룡의 오른편에서 숱한 격전을 치른 역전의 무사 혁무진! 그게 바로 접니다.”
 94|
 95|그리고 정확히 한 시진 후, 역전의 무사 혁무진은 구토와 함께 쓰러졌다.
 96|
 97|“우웨에에엑!”
 98|
 99|“헉, 무진아!”
100|
101|“이게 무슨 일인가!”
102|
103|“남 노인! 무진이가 쓰러졌습니다!”
104|
105|“내가 아무리 늙었어도 쓰러진 건 다 보여. 혹시 모기에 물렸나?”
106|
107|“쿨럭, 예에. 한 시진 전쯤에 푸른 줄무늬가 있는 놈한테…….”
108|
109|“푸른 줄무늬? 그것도 한 시진 전? 해독제. 빨리 해독제 가져와!”
110|
111|다행히 역전의 무사를 일으켜 세우는 것은 그리 어렵지 않았다.
112|
113|내게는 사천당가의 신물인 만독지환(萬毒指環)과 퀘스트 보상으로 받은 해독제가 오십 개나 있었으니까.
114|
115|하지만 그렇다고 해서 안심할 상황은 아니었다.
116|
117|“본래는 수십 마리씩 무리를 지어 몰려다니며 맹수까지 사냥하는 놈들이지. 한 시진만 더 늦었어도 이 세상 사람이 아니었을 걸세.”
118|
119|남호의 엄중한 경고와 함께 우리는 다시 이동을 시작했다. 한족이라면 눈깔을 뒤집고 달려드는 이민족들의 눈을 피해 더 깊숙하고 은밀한 곳으로.
120|
121|그리고 그건, 더욱 위험한 곳으로 향하고 있다는 뜻이었다.
122|
123|“태산이! 태산이 배가 너무 아프다! 찢어질 것 같다!”
124|
125|“남 노인!”
126|
127|“또 뭘 처먹었어!”
128|
129|“태산이. 배가 고파서 나무에 피어 있던 붉은 버섯을 뜯어 먹었다.”
130|
131|“이런 천하의 개돼지 같은 놈을 보았나! 내 그토록 주의를 줬거늘, 단순히 허기가 졌다고 해서 호랑이도 못 버티는 혈생균(血牲菌)을 처먹어? 이건 해독제도 안 통해!”
132|
133|극대노를 몸소 시전한 남호였지만 그의 분노는 이내 당혹스러움으로 바뀌었다.
134|
135|호랑이도 못 버틴다는 혈생균인지 뭔지를 처먹은 태산이 풀숲으로 들어가 거사를 치른 뒤에 씻은 듯이 나았기 때문이었다.
136|
137|“태산이. 다 싸고 나니까 편안하다. 이제 괜찮다.”
138|
139|“……저놈. 사람 맞나?”
140|
141|진심이 담긴 남호의 물음에 잠시 고민하던 사마표가 자신 없는 목소리로 대답했다.
142|
143|“아마도 그럴 거요.”
144|
145|“태산이. 속이 비니까 다시 배가 고프다.”
146|
147|“내 천지신명께 맹세컨대, 두 번 다시 버섯 따위를 처먹었다가는 영영 허기질 일이 없게 될 줄 알아라.”
148|
149|“오오. 태산이. 솔깃하다.”
150|
151|“……후회되는군. 만약 무공을 익혔다면 지금쯤 저놈을 일장에 쳐 죽였을 텐데.”
152|
153|늙은 은영각 요원의 한탄을 뒤로하고 걸음은 계속해서 이어졌다.
154|
155|발길이 닿는 곳마다 빽빽한 밀림과 습하면서도 무더운 열기가 우리를 기다리고 있었고, 우거진 풀숲과 늪지대 곳곳에 도사린 맹수들의 눈동자는 샛노랗게 빛났다.
156|
157|‘혹시 남만이 아니라 아마존에 온 건가.’
158|
159|말 그대로 개똥 땅.
160|
161|뭔 놈의 동네가 이 모양인지, 호랑이가 대학가 원룸촌 길냥이보다 많이 보이고 악어는 청계천 올챙이처럼 우글거린다.
162|
163|물론 이마저도 향만 맡아도 훅 간다는 기화독초(奇花毒草)와 제 몸통보다 큰 독침을 달고 다니는 벌에 비교하면 애교 수준이었다.
164|
165|그나마 맹수들은 덩치가 큰 탓에 눈에 띄기라도 하니까.
166|
167|영인을 떠난 지 하루 이틀 만에 혁무진이 앓는 소리를 한 것에는 그만한 이유가 있었다.
168|
169|“남만야수궁이고 나발이고, 내일모레쯤 뒈질 것 같습니다.”
170|
171|내일모레까진 아니더라도, 나흘 후에는 생명이 위험해 보이긴 했다. 첫날에만 네 번 정도 중독된 녀석은 지난 이틀 사이 피골이 상접 해 있었으니까.
172|
173|산서성도 중원의 시각으로는 변경(邊境)에 속한 곳이지만, 남만의 수준은 예상했던 범위를 훌쩍 뛰어넘었다.
174|
175|“이러지 말고 다른 길로 가면 안 됩니까? 좀 후지고 험하긴 해도 이곳에 비하면 완전 꽃길이나 다름없을 텐데.”
176|
177|남만에도 길이 아예 없는 것은 아니다.
178|
179|중원에 비하면 심하게 낙후되었지만, 남만에 자리 잡은 수십, 수백여 갈래의 이민족들은 저마다의 구역을 정하고 분쟁이 일어나지 않는 선에서 왕래를 하는 경우도 그리 드물지는 않다고 들었다.
180|
181|그러나 간절한 혁무진의 청원에도 남호의 대답은 단호했다.
182|
183|“불가(不可). 그 이유는 자네도 알겠지?”
184|
185|“저희를 죽이고 싶어서 환장한 이민족 때문이라면, 차라리 시원하게 맞서 싸우고 말겠습니다. 만약 대화로 잘 풀 수 있다면 그걸로 좋은 거고요.”
186|
187|“대화?”
188|
189|꿈과 희망이 가득한 혁무진의 대답에 남호가 눈을 깜빡였다.
190|
191|“진심인가?”
192|
193|“물론입니다.”
194|
195|“마을 하나가 사라졌네. 호의로 한족들을 맞이한 이백여 명이 남녀노소 가리지 않고 도륙당했다고. 그런데 대화가 통할 것 같나?”
196|
197|“……아뇨. 사실 진심은 아니었습니다.”
198|
199|“이제야 좀 솔직해졌군. 좋아, 그럼 닥치고 가자고.”
200|
201|“옙.”
202|
203|혁가 놈. 빛보다 빠른 태세 전환 보소.
204|
205|하지만 이번만큼은 남호의 말이 구구절절 옳았다.
206|
207|당장 우리에게 덤벼드는 이민족과 맞서 싸운다는 소리는 남만 전체와 전쟁을 치르겠다는 말과 동의어다.
208|
209|평소에는 서로를 향해 으르렁거리다가도, 외부의 적이 나타난다면 언제 그랬냐는 듯이 똘똘 뭉치는 것이 남만의 특징 중 하나라고 했다.
210|
211|‘그러니 정마대전 당시의 마교조차 남만을 완전히 정벌하지 못했겠지.’
212|
213|한때 천하의 절반을 집어삼켰던 마교의 십만마병(十萬魔兵)도 남만 외곽에 깃발만 꽂고 물러나는 것이 고작이었다.
214|
215|남만의 지독한 풍토병과 험난한 지형. 그리고 온갖 맹수와 독물이 득실거리는 이 밀림에 그 이상 깊숙이 들어선다면 득보다 실이 클 것을 알았기 때문이다.
216|
217|‘그렇다고 신상을 까고 돌아다닐 수도 없는 노릇이고.’
218|
219|한족 혐오 감정이 팽배한 이민족들이 그 정도로 적대감을 누그러트릴지도 의문이지만, 더 중요한 건 바로 남만 어딘가에 도사리고 있을 암천(暗天)의 존재였다.
220|
221|‘놈들은 반드시 남만을 노린다. 일이 터지는 건 시간문제일 뿐이야.’
222|
223|이건 확신에 가까운 짐작이었다. 괜히 우리가 무림맹 총단이 위치한 하남에서부터 밤손님처럼 은밀하게 이동한 것이 아니다.
224|
225|남만까지 오는 과정에서 부득이하게 수룡채의 수적들에게 신분을 노출하긴 했지만, 입단속도 철저히 했다.
226|
227|지난번 사천행에서 인연을 쌓았던 아미파와 청성파, 그리고 사천당가에 굳이 연통을 넣지 않았던 이유도 그 때문이었다.
228|
229|하지만 우리가 이민족들에게 신분을 밝힌다면 그동안의 노력이 전부 허사가 된다.
230|
231|보이지 않던 비수가 코앞까지 다가온 것을 깨달은 암천은 계획에 더욱 박차를 가할 테고, ‘균열’과 함께 재앙의 문이 열릴 테니까.
232|
233|‘신분을 밝히는 것은 최소한 남만야수궁에 도착한 뒤여야 해.’
234|
235|남만야수궁의 궁주인 야수묘왕(野獸苗王)은 정마대전에 참전했던 전력이 있을뿐더러, 적천강과 열화문에 호의를 품고 있다고 들었다.
236|
237|일의 경중이나 남만에서 차지하는 위상으로 따져 보아도, 눈깔이 뒤집힌 여타 이민족들보다는 훨씬 말이 통하는 상대인 것이다.
238|
239|‘그나저나 천마표국인지 뭔지 하는 놈들 때문에 우리한테까지 똥이 튀네.’
240|
241|어물전 망신은 꼴뚜기가 다 시킨다더니, 괜히 동족 패키지 상품으로 같이 묶여서 나나 화룡각 대원들 이미지만 개박살이 났다.
242|
243|심지어 나는 한족 출신도 아닌데.
244|
245|‘……이게 폰한족인지 뭔지 하는 그거냐.’
246|
247|더럽게 억울해도 방법이 없다.
248|

It was badly underdeveloped compared to the Central Plains, but I’d heard that the dozens, perhaps hundreds, of non-Han peoples settled here each had their own territory. Travel between them wasn’t particularly rare, so long as it didn’t cause disputes.

[P67]
Despite Mujin’s desperate plea, Namho was firm.

[P68]
“Impossible. You know why.”

[P69]
“If it’s because the locals are dying to kill us, I’d rather face them head-on. And if we can talk things out, all the better.”

[P70]
“Talk?”

[P71]
Namho blinked at Mujin’s hopeful answer.

[P72]
“Are you serious?”

[P73]
“Of course.”

[P74]
“An entire village vanished. Some two hundred people welcomed Han Chinese in good faith and were slaughtered, young and old alike. Do you think they’ll want to talk?”

[P75]
“…No. I wasn’t actually serious.”

[P76]
“Now you’re being honest. Good. Then shut up and walk.”

[P77]
“Yes, sir.”

[P78]
*Look at him change his tune faster than light.*

[P79]
But this time, Namho was right about everything.

[P80]
Fighting the non-Han peoples who attacked us would amount to declaring war on all of Nanman. They might snarl at one another ordinarily, but when an outsider appeared, they united as if their quarrels had never existed.

[P81]
*No wonder even the Demonic Cult failed to conquer all of Nanman during the Great Faction War.*

[P82]
The Cult’s hundred thousand demonic soldiers had once swallowed half the world, yet all they managed here was to plant their flags on Nanman’s outskirts before withdrawing.

[P83]
They knew that going any deeper into a jungle rife with brutal endemic diseases, treacherous terrain, predators, and venomous beasts would cost more than it gained them.

[P84]
*And we can’t exactly go around announcing who we are.*

[P85]
I doubted the non-Han peoples’ hatred of Han Chinese would ease just because we told them our names. More importantly, Dark Heaven was lurking somewhere in Nanman.

[P86]
*They’re definitely targeting this place. It’s only a matter of time before something happens.*

[P87]
I was almost certain. We hadn’t traveled like thieves in the night all the way from Henan, where the Murim Alliance headquarters stood, for nothing.

[P88]
We’d had to reveal our identities to the bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold on our way here, but we’d made sure they kept quiet. It was also why we hadn’t contacted the Emei Sect, the Qingcheng Sect, or the Sichuan Tang Clan, despite the ties we’d made on our last trip to Sichuan.

[P89]
If we revealed ourselves to the non-Han peoples now, all that effort would go to waste.

[P90]
Dark Heaven would realize an unseen dagger had come right up to its nose and rush its plans forward. Then the rift would open, and with it the door to disaster.

[P91]
*We can’t reveal who we are until we reach the Nanman Beast Palace at the very least.*

[P92]
The Beast Miao King, lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, had fought in the Great Faction War. I’d also heard he was well disposed toward Jeok Cheongang and the Fire Gate Clan.

[P93]
Given the importance of our business and his standing in Nanman, he was far more likely to listen than the other non-Han peoples, who were beside themselves with anger.

[P94]
*And thanks to those Heavenly Demon Escort Bureau bastards, we’re getting shit splashed on us too.*

[P95]
One squid makes the whole fish market look bad, as they say. We’d been bundled together with them in the same Han Chinese package, and the Fire Dragon Pavilion’s reputation—mine included—was shot.

[P96]
I wasn’t even Han Chinese.

[P97]
*…Does this make me a fake Han Chinese or what?*

[P98]
It was unfair as hell, but there was nothing I could do. I could tell the locals, “Actually, I’m not Han Chinese. I’m Korean. South, not North,” and they wouldn’t understand a word.

[P99]
Besides, when I’d gotten homesick during training at Mount Jiuhua and drawn the Korean flag, Jeok Cheongang had said just one thing.

[P100]
*“Wudang?”*

[P101]
*“No.”*

[P102]
*“It’s obviously taiji. What kind of bullshit are you talking? Taiji means Wudang.”*

[P103]
*“Taiji means Korea.”*

[P104]
*“What’s Korea?”*

[P105]
*“That’s… Never mind. You don’t need to know, Old Master.”*

[P106]
*“Add two hundred geun of iron balls.”*

[P107]
*“…Two hundred geun? Why?”*

[P108]
*“You don’t need to know.”*

[P109]
Just remembering it brought tears to my eyes.

[P110]
It felt like only yesterday I’d been suffering in this distant land of another dimension. The miserable part was that the suffering never stopped.

[P111]
“Whew.”

[P112]
Namho glared at me when he heard me sigh.

[P113]
“What? Do you want to go down there and talk things out too? Or would you rather have a good, hard fight with the locals?”

[P114]
“…Where did that come from? I don’t want to do either.”

[P115]
“That’s a relief.”

[P116]
We’d already had plenty of fights, and there would be plenty more. How many predators were prowling around us right now, making those cries?

[P117]
I scanned the dense jungle and swampland, then asked Namho, “How much farther?”

[P118]
“Three days if we’re quick. Six if we’re not.”

[P119]
“That’s a lot farther than I expected.”

[P120]
“Given that we have to stay out of sight, even that’s quick.”

[P121]
Namho, looking older by the hour, patted his lower back and set off again.

[P122]
“Don’t slow down for a moment from here on. If we cross Ailao Mountain today, we can reach the Nanman Beast Palace in four days at the latest.”

[P123]
He was right.

[P124]
Exactly four days later, as we crossed a high mountain peak, we spotted a massive structure in the distance, shrouded in thick clouds and mist.

[P125]
“The Nanman Beast Palace…”

[P126]
The words slipped from someone’s lips and carried away on a wind that blew in from somewhere.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.

[P3]

[P4]

[P5]

[P6]

[P7]

[P8]

[P9]

[P10]

[P11]
Destination, huh?

[P12]

[P13]
The space above us was, quite literally, an empty void where there was nothing at all.

[P14]

[P20]
Nanman was an expansive land, but it was also unbelievably rugged.

[P21]
In terms of land area, it was smaller than Sichuan, but the effort required to travel through it was incomparable to anything in the Central Plains.

[P22]
“The Pavilion Master once said this: ten li in Nanman is the same as a hundred li in the Central Plains.”

[P23]
Anyone who couldn’t understand Namho’s words had never set foot in Nanman.

[P24]
Because in only half a day, the Fire Dragon Pavilion members and I had learned exactly what a damnable place Nanman was.

[P25]
Bzzzzzt. Smack!

[P26]
“Mujin, what was that sound just now?”

[P27]
“It was nothing. Just a mosquito. My nape suddenly stung, so I wondered what it was.”

[P28]
“Oh, really? Still, be careful. You never know. Should I call Elder Namho and ask him about it?”

[P29]
“Come on, Captain. What do you take me for, a child? Hyuk Mujin, a battle-hardened warrior who has fought countless fierce battles at the right hand of the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon! That’s me.”

[P30]

[P31]
“Bleeaaagh!”

[P32]
“Gasp, Mujin!”

[P33]
“What happened?”

[P34]
“Elder Namho! Mujin has collapsed!”

[P35]

[P36]
“Cough, yes. About one shichen ago, by one with blue stripes…”

[P37]
“Blue stripes? And it was one shichen ago? An antidote. Hurry and bring me an antidote!”

[P38]
Fortunately, getting the battle-hardened warrior back on his feet wasn’t particularly difficult.

[P39]
I had the Myriad-Poison Ring, a treasured item of the Sichuan Tang Clan, as well as fifty antidotes I had received as Quest rewards.

[P40]
But that didn’t mean we could let our guard down.

[P41]
“They normally swarm together in groups of dozens and even hunt predators. If we’d been one shichen later, he wouldn’t be among the living anymore.”

[P42]
With Namho’s stern warning ringing in our ears, we resumed moving deeper into the secluded land, avoiding the eyes of the non-Han peoples who charged at Han Chinese the moment they saw them.

[P43]
And that meant we were heading into an even more dangerous place.

[P44]
“Taishan! Taishan’s stomach hurts too much! It feels like it’s being torn apart!”

[P45]
“Elder Namho!”

[P46]
“What did you eat this time?”

[P47]
“Taishan was hungry, so Taishan picked and ate the red mushrooms growing on a tree.”

[P48]
“What kind of dog and pig bastard are you? After all the warnings I gave you, you ate blood-feeding fungus that even a tiger couldn’t withstand just because you were hungry? Antidotes won’t work on this!”

[P49]
Namho personally unleashed a fit of absolute fury, but his anger soon turned into bewilderment.

[P50]
Taishan had eaten whatever this blood-feeding fungus was—the kind that even a tiger supposedly couldn’t survive—and then gone into the brush to do his business. Afterward, he came back looking perfectly fine.

[P51]
“Taishan. Feels better after shitting it all out. Taishan is fine now.”

[P52]
“……Is that thing even human?”

[P53]
After a moment of thought, Sama Pyo answered in an uncertain voice.

[P54]
“Probably.”

[P55]
“Taishan is hungry again now that Taishan’s stomach is empty.”

[P56]
“I swear by heaven and earth, if you ever eat another mushroom, you’d better be prepared never to feel hunger again.”

[P57]
“Oh. Taishan. Tempting.”

[P58]
“……I regret everything. If I had learned martial arts, I would have killed that bastard with a single palm strike by now.”

[P59]
We continued on our way, leaving the old Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent to lament behind us.

[P60]
Dense jungle and humid, sweltering heat awaited us at every step, while the eyes of predators lurking throughout the overgrown brush and swamplands glowed a vivid yellow.

[P61]
*Did we come to Nanman, or did we somehow end up in the Amazon?*

[P62]
What a goddamn shithole.

[P63]
What kind of place was this? Tigers were more common than stray cats in a university neighborhood full of studio apartments, and crocodiles teemed like tadpoles in Cheonggyecheon.

[P64]
Of course, even that was child’s play compared to the strange poisonous flowers and plants that could knock you out from their scent alone, or the bees that flew around with stingers larger than their own bodies.

[P65]
At least the predators were large enough to be seen.

[P66]
There was a reason Hyuk Mujin had started groaning only a day or two after leaving Yeongin.

[P67]
“To hell with the Nanman Beast Palace. I think I’ll be dead by the day after tomorrow.”

[P68]
Even if it wasn’t by the day after tomorrow, he did look as if his life would be in danger four days from now. He had been poisoned about four times on the first day alone, and over the past two days he had become skin and bones.

[P69]
Shanxi Province was considered a borderland from the Central Plains’ perspective, but Nanman had gone far beyond anything we had expected.

[P70]
“Can’t we take another route? It might be a little run-down and rough, but compared to this place, it’d practically be a flower-lined path.”

[P71]
It wasn’t as if there were no paths in Nanman at all.

[P72]
Though it was severely underdeveloped compared to the Central Plains, I had heard that the dozens or even hundreds of non-Han peoples who had settled in Nanman each claimed their own territories, and that it wasn’t particularly unusual for them to travel back and forth so long as they didn’t cause disputes.

[P73]
But despite Hyuk Mujin’s desperate plea, Namho’s answer was firm.

[P74]
“Impossible. You know the reason, don’t you?”

[P75]
“If it’s because of the non-Han peoples who are dying to kill us, I’d rather just face them head-on. If we can settle things through conversation, then all the better.”

[P76]
“Conversation?”

[P77]
Namho blinked at Hyuk Mujin’s answer, which was full of dreams and hope.

[P78]
“Are you serious?”

[P79]
“Of course.”

[P80]
“An entire village disappeared. More than two hundred people who had welcomed Han Chinese with goodwill were slaughtered, regardless of age or sex. Do you think conversation will work?”

[P81]
“……No. Actually, I wasn’t serious.”

[P82]
“You’re finally being honest. Fine, then shut up and keep moving.”

[P83]
“Yes, sir.”

[P84]
*Look at Captain Hyuk’s lightning-fast change of attitude.*

[P85]
But this time, Namho was completely right.

[P86]
Saying that we would fight the non-Han people who attacked us was the same as declaring war on all of Nanman.

[P87]
They normally snarled at one another, but one of Nanman’s defining traits was that they would unite as if nothing had happened whenever an external enemy appeared.

[P88]
*That must be why even the Demonic Cult couldn’t completely conquer Nanman during the Great Faction War.*

[P89]
The hundred thousand demonic soldiers of the Demonic Cult, who had once swallowed half the world, had only been able to plant their flags around Nanman’s outskirts before withdrawing.

[P90]
They knew that if they went any deeper into this jungle, with its brutal endemic diseases, treacherous terrain, and countless predators and venomous beasts, the losses would outweigh the gains.

[P91]
*But it’s not as if we can go around revealing our identities, either.*

[P92]
It was questionable whether the non-Han peoples, whose hatred of Han Chinese ran so deep, would lower their hostility that easily. But more important was the presence of Dark Heaven, which was surely lurking somewhere in Nanman.

[P93]
*They’re definitely targeting Nanman. It’s only a matter of time before something happens.*

[P94]
This was an assumption bordering on certainty. There was a reason we had traveled secretly, like nighttime thieves, all the way from Henan, where the Murim Alliance headquarters was located.

[P95]
We had been forced to reveal our identities to the bandits of the Water Dragon Stronghold on the way to Nanman, but we had also made certain that they kept their mouths shut.

[P96]
That was why we hadn’t sent word to the Emei Sect, the Qingcheng Sect, or the Sichuan Tang Clan, despite the ties we had formed during our previous journey to Sichuan.

[P97]
But if we revealed our identities to the non-Han peoples, all our efforts would be wasted.

[P98]
Dark Heaven would realize that the unseen dagger was right under its nose and accelerate its plans even further. Then the door to disaster would open along with the rift.

[P99]
*We can’t reveal our identities until at least after we arrive at the Nanman Beast Palace.*

[P100]
The Beast Miao King, lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, had participated in the Great Faction War, and I had heard that he held goodwill toward Jeok Cheongang and the Fire Gate Clan.

[P101]
Considering both the importance of our business and the position he occupied in Nanman, he was far more likely to listen than the other non-Han peoples with their eyes turned red.

[P102]
*Still, we’re getting shit splattered on us because of those Heavenly Demon Escort Bureau bastards or whatever they are.*

[P103]
They say the squid is the one that shames the fish market. We had been lumped together with them as part of the same Han Chinese package, and the image of both me and the Fire Dragon Pavilion members had been completely ruined.

[P104]
I wasn’t even Han Chinese.

[P105]
*……Is this what they call being a fake Han Chinese?*

[P106]
It was incredibly unfair, but there was nothing I could do.

[P107]
Even if I went up to the non-Han peoples of Nanman and pulled some shit like, “Actually, I’m not Han Chinese. I’m Korean. South, not North,” there was no way they’d understand.

[P108]
Besides, when I had gotten homesick during our training at Mount Jiuhua and drawn the Korean flag, Jeok Cheongang had said only one thing.

[P109]
*“Wudang?”*

[P110]
*“No.”*

[P111]
*“Anyone can see it’s taiji. What kind of bullshit are you spouting? If it’s taiji, it’s Wudang.”*

[P112]
*“If it’s taiji, it’s Korea.”*

[P113]
*“What’s Korea?”*

[P114]
*“That’s… Never mind. You don’t need to know, Old Master.”*

[P115]
*“An extra two hundred geun of iron balls.”*

[P116]
*“……Two hundred geun? Why?”*

[P117]
*“You don’t need to know.”*

[P118]
Even remembering it brought tears to my eyes.

[P119]
It felt like only yesterday that I had been suffering in this distant land of another dimension, yet the fact that the suffering was still ongoing was enough to make me despair.

[P120]
“Whew.”

[P121]
At the sight of me sighing, Namho glared fiercely.

[P122]
“What? Do you also want to go down there and settle things through conversation right now? Or would you rather throw down with the non-Han peoples?”

[P123]
“……Why are you suddenly revving up like that? I have absolutely no desire to do either.”

[P124]
“That’s a relief.”

[P125]
There had already been plenty of chances to throw down with someone, and there would be plenty more in the future. Even now, several predators were wandering around us, letting out their cries.

[P126]
After surveying the densely packed jungle and swamplands, I asked Namho,

[P127]
“How much farther?”

[P128]
“Three days if we’re quick. Six days at most.”

[P129]
“That’s much farther than I expected.”

[P130]
“Considering that we have to travel while avoiding prying eyes, even that is a short estimate.”

[P131]
Namho, whose face had aged noticeably, patted his lower back before starting to walk again.

[P132]
“From now on, don’t slow your pace for even a moment. If we cross Ailao Mountain today, we’ll be able to reach the Nanman Beast Palace in four days at the latest.”

[P133]
Namho’s words proved true.

[P134]
Exactly four days later, as we passed over a high mountain peak, we spotted a massive structure in the distance, shrouded in deep clouds and mist.

[P135]
“The Nanman Beast Palace…”

[P136]
The voice that slipped from someone’s lips spread on a wind that had blown in from somewhere.

[P137]
[^1]: A shichen is approximately two hours, while a li is approximately half a kilometer. A geun is a traditional unit of weight roughly equal to 600 grams.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
